page_out_of_date_or_wrong.issue: The page says the only controlled test was PACE's APT arm. RECOVER-ENERGIZE structured pacing vs usual care (NCT06404073, n=298, long COVID) reduced how often PEM happened (-0.46, CI -0.65 to -0.27) and how severe it was. It is the first positive randomised trial of pacing.

The page calls the Nacul trial 'presented May 2026, unpublished'. It is now a medRxiv preprint, Oct 2026 (DOI 10.64898/2026.10.22.26363582; NCT05430152): no difference in fatigue (FSS), pain, symptoms, steps or quality of life at 16 weeks. The cited reference should be updated.

The page cites a 2024 company release for the long COVID trial. ClinicalTrials.gov now has posted results (NCT05592418, n=80): the change in PROMIS fatigue was essentially the same on drug and placebo. The 1994 placebo-controlled RCT (n=92, PMID 8148460, positive on Karnofsky score and treadmill work) is not cited.

PAuSing-pCF is listed as a pending preprint. It is now published in NIHR Open Research (DOI 10.3310/nihropenres.14236.1, n=114): fatigue at 8 weeks did not differ from sham or placebo. It should move from 'pending' into the evidence line. Also pending: NCT07190105 (n=546, finished Dec 2025, not reported).

The page says 'creatine has only a 12-person long-COVID RCT'. That is out of date: a 3-arm placebo-controlled RCT (n=67, PMID 41958909) found that 6 g/day improved fatigue and muscle strength (18 g did not). There are also two other small long COVID creatine RCTs (PMID 38099612, 38684388) and an open-label ME/CFS MRS study (PMID 39408275, n=11). NCT05703074 (nicotinamide riboside plus mind-body therapy, n=310, completed Sep 2024) has not reported.

The page says plasma exchange has only case reports. There is a sham-controlled plasma exchange RCT (NCT05445674, n=50, posted results): safe, but no difference on any efficacy outcome. That adds to the negative evidence. On BC007, the page says it failed a 114-person unpublished company trial. The database has the 30-person reCOVer crossover published as positive (CTIS 2022-001781-35) and the phase 2 RCT NCT05911009 (n=119, completed Jun 2024) with no posted results and no paper. The page should cite the registry record and make clear the failure is not yet in a publication or posted results.

Only methylphenidate is cited. Missing: lisdexamfetamine vs placebo (NCT01071044, n=26), which improved executive function and fatigue, and solriamfetol vs placebo (NCT04622293, n=44), which improved fatigue at week 8 but not week 6. Also NCT01966276 (methylphenidate plus nutrient formula, n=134 planned, completed 2014): no results ever reported.

The evidence line rests on PACE alone. The database has about 40 other randomised CBT or psychological trials in ME/CFS: FITNET-NHS (n=~240), FINE (n=296, null at 70 weeks), Dutch group, internet and stepped-care CBT, and CBSM, which helped only the high-PEM subgroup. Most are unblinded and use self-rated outcomes, and many are positive. The page's conclusion can stand, but it should say that the wider body exists and why it is discounted (unblinded subjective outcomes, few objective measures).

The page could cite MAGENTA (ISRCTN23962803, paediatric, GET no better than activity management) and GETSET (ISRCTN22975026, guided self-help GET, a self-rated gain). PACE alone is not the full trial base.

This matches the database. Add the terminated subcutaneous IgPro20 trial in post-COVID POTS (NCT06524739, n=16, uninterpretable). RECOVER-AUTONOMIC IVIG (NCT06305793, n=200) has finished, with no results posted or published.

The page cites the RECOVER-AUTONOMIC ACC 2026 presentation. The database has no paper or posted results for NCT06305806 yet, so this could not be checked. NCT05481177 (ivabradine nested RCT, n=250, completed Sep 2024) has not reported.
There are two unreported long COVID steroid RCTs: prednisolone plus B vitamins (NCT05638633, n=321, completed Jan 2025) and methylprednisolone vs placebo (NCT05986422, terminated, n=96).

FMT matches the database. The probiotics entry (one 39-person RCT) is missing several placebo RCTs that have not reported: NCT04741841 (GutMagnific, ME/CFS, n=74, completed 2021), NCT05975034 (long COVID, n=240 planned, completion Dec 2023, status UNKNOWN), NCT05813899 (L. paracasei PS23, terminated). Also PURE-LC (NCT06643299, n=194), completed Jul 2026.
The valacyclovir plus celecoxib pilot RCT (NCT06316843, n=59) was completed Oct 2024 and has not reported. The page mentions only the planned trial NCT07597902.

Add the sodium oxybate placebo RCTs (SAFFE NCT02055898, n=13, more slow-wave sleep but no daytime gain; NCT00498485, terminated, n=17). A second melatonin plus zinc RCT (NCT05454683, n=106 planned, completion Sep 2024) has not reported.

The page says there is no randomised trial. Two have not reported: NCT04740736 (ME/CFS, saline infusion vs placebo in a PEM study, n=106, completed Jul 2025) and NCT02854683 (oral rehydration vs IV saline crossover, status UNKNOWN, completion 2021).
This matches the database. NCT05668039 is still not reported (status UNKNOWN, primary completion Apr 2024).

The page cites STAR-CO NCT06253806, which is not in the database (it was not returned by the ME/CFS or long COVID searches; check it is the right ID). The database has two placebo-controlled RCTs that are recruiting (NCT07374562; a cervicothoracic sympathetic chain block vs saline, NCT07468604) and an open-label dual-block study, NCT05638620 (n=20, COMPASS-31 down 38%).

treatments_with_trials_but_no_page_entry.evidence: Two placebo RCTs, both favourable: an adaptive fluvoxamine/metformin trial (NCT06128967, n=399), where fluvoxamine reduced fatigue at days 60 and 90, and NCT05874037 (n=137), with a bigger fall in symptom score but no p-value posted. Another RCT is recruiting (NCT07359482).
Null in the adaptive trial (NCT06128967) and in a Korean RCT (KCT0009342, n=396). NCT07280572 (n=1,250) is enrolling.
Null in a placebo RCT (CTRI/2021/11/038234, n=346). In STIMULATE-ICP (open-label) it reduced fatigue slightly. NCT07280572 is ongoing.
Placebo RCT, n=203: no improvement in fatigue.
Placebo RCT in post-COVID POTS, n=53: no benefit (COMPASS-31 -14.4 vs -16.0). The extension study was terminated.
REGENECYTE cord blood vs placebo (NCT05682560, n=30): positive on fatigue, but small and industry-run. NCT06492798 (n=76) is overdue. Five MSC trials were withdrawn.

Placebo RCT for post-COVID asthenia, n=676: FSS fell 16.5 vs 14.0. The difference is significant but small, and the trial was industry-sponsored. This is the largest positive blinded trial in the database.
Placebo RCT, n=149: no significant gain on the primary cognitive measure (DSST).
Placebo RCT, n=52: no effect on fatigue or brain fog.

PYCNOVID (n=153) was null. Smaller positive RCTs: quercetin phytosome (n=78), cocoa flavonoids (FLALOC, n=46), high-polyphenol chocolate (n=10). The page's fibre-polyphenols entry says there is no treatment trial.
RECOVER-NEURO (NCT05965739, n=328): no benefit from BrainHQ, PASC-CoRE or tDCS. Single-centre tDCS trials are split (NCT04876417 null; NCT05389592 small gains).
Open-label RCT positive on FSS (PMID 38228731). The placebo RCT NCT06055244 (n=64) finished in Dec 2025 and has not reported. A 1997 ME/CFS RCT found it poorly tolerated.
Placebo RCT in ME/CFS, n=434: no benefit on any outcome.
Both null in placebo RCTs of long COVID (n=272 and n=177).

treatments_with_trials_but_no_page_entry.treatment: structured rehabilitation programmes for long COVID
treatments_with_trials_but_no_page_entry.evidence: REGAIN online group rehab (ISRCTN11466448, n=585) improved quality of life. SIPCOV (n=314) and personalised resistance exercise (n=233) were positive, and PEM did not increase. All were unblinded. The page has no long COVID rehab entry separate from GET.
A phase 3 long COVID RCT is registered in CTIS (2023-504087-42-00, n=260 planned). No results yet.
